done.what: (earlier agent) The changes list's 'more below' fade is set only when the last chip's own box passes the list's foot (2px tolerance), not from scrollHeight; the chip's × hit area now stays inside the 28px chip (inset -4/-4/-4/-8), so nothing overflows. Measured on the pre-D build with the new CSS: 1–2 chips sh=ch=28, 3 chips 64/64 at 1440; at 1280/1366 the 1.5-row cap cuts the third chip and the fade shows only then. Also covers new:editor-visual:fade on every list and new:surfaces-furniture:last chip always fades.

(earlier agent) The foot's rows never shrink (.foot > * { flex-shrink: 0 }) and Generate keeps a 36px floor, so the scroll takes the overflow on a short laptop (new:style-light-tools:Generate collapses to 20px) — measured 36px at 1366×768 and 1280×800 with a long focused note. (this run) The remaining part: picking Empty the room or Furnish the room scrolls the panel so the options under the card come into view (never the chosen card past its top; a panel reopened on a tool already picked stays put; smooth unless reduced motion). The panel body carries data-viz-panel-body for it.

(earlier agent) Describe a change draws its box on the field around a padding-less textarea, so every resting height is whole 20px lines and a second line can never peek; the tray's caption is visually hidden (still the textarea's name); a press on the field's padding focuses the words. The compact mic's resting position keys on the textarea's focus like the others. Dedupes new:editor-visual 2, engine 3, surfaces-furniture 2, phone-tablet 3, motion-a11y 4, style-light-tools 2, fresh-desktop 6, fresh-tablet 14, fresh-phone 5.

(earlier agent) A style card's materials are listed one to a line beside their chip, named in full (no clamp). (this run) The style cards sit on a subgrid (inside @supports), so across a row the pictures, names, descriptions and material lists each start level whatever wraps. Checked at 1440, 1025, 390 and 320: no name cut.

(earlier agent) Every table reads as a table (coffee / side / end / console / dining table, desk → table_restaurant; the Tables fallback too); a TV console stays storage. All glyph names are in the subset (checked).

(earlier agent) The surface header, ticks and rows read only picks whose material still resolves — no 'Now: … · →' with an empty target. The Surfaces tab dot is the editor's (its marks now count only resolvable picks).

(earlier agent) D6: the picker's 'Now' line reads '{name} (renamed since)' when the version's snapshot name differs from the material's current one. (this run) '(recoloured since)' when only the colour changed; Recent now shows the studio's and the design's own materials (it resolved catalogue ids only), and a studio material's chip wears the pattern the render gives it (resolveMaterial). The delete-confirm 'Used in n designs' is the gallery's (notDone).

(this run) Part (1): the picker's swatches and the rail's surface rows share one chip (useSwatchCss): a printed motif (wallpaper prints, tile bonds — stripe, botanical, deco, wave, floral, geometric, brick, subway, hex, penny, herringbone, chevron, cement…) wears the engine's own tile at its real repeat via version-facts' finishChip — the moodboard's chip — after hydration; textures (marble, boards, concrete) keep the CSS chip (drawing them costs ~140ms). Compared all 29 tiled swatches side by side against the CSS sketches (tiles-cmp.png).
(earlier agent) A reference photo's remove × is a white round chip with elevation-1 and a 36px target — readable on light, mid and dark photos (checked).
(this run) The density line ends with its own full stop and says what the render does today in plain words; 'empty it first' shows only where this version can be emptied and isn't.

crossFileRequests.ref: new:fresh-desktop:Furnish says Empty first though an emptied version exists
crossFileRequests.change: Wire the new props. Near `tools`: `const emptiedV = tools && !tools.canFurnish && tools.canEmpty ? [...all].reverse().find((v) => v.finishes.emptied && !v.deleted && v.key !== viewKey) ?? null : null; const emptiedLink = emptiedV ? { n: emptiedV.n, onOpen: () => setView(emptiedV.key) } : null`. Pass `emptied={emptiedLink}` to <ToolsPanel …>, and to <GenerateFooter …> in footer(): `reasonLink={pending.tool === 'furnish' && emptiedLink && !footIntent.kind ? { text: 'Furnish works on an emptied version —', label: `open V${emptiedLink.n}`, onPress: emptiedLink.onOpen } : null}` (invented copy, same words as the Tools panel).

(1) The rail's rows add var(--viz-inset-l/-r, 0px) to their padding; while the editor paints the notch insets with env() on .rail / .goDock / .fold, do NOT also define --viz-inset-l/-r on an ancestor of the rail or the dock, or those rows get the inset twice (stage.module.css / versions-strip.module.css read the same variables). (2) Optional: key the FAB rule on the rail's own hook `.editor:has([data-viz-knobs]) .fab { display: none; }` instead of the button's aria-label text.

Keep `export function finishChip(f: Pick<FinishedSurface, 'hex' | 'pattern'>, imageUrl?: string | null): string` exported with this signature — panels/material-picker.tsx imports it so the picker, the rail rows and the moodboard draw one tile. (Better home later: move patternUrl / finishChip into lib/visualizer/patterns.ts.)
